brief.meaningEn: Be harmed or affected by a conflict between other people.
brief.meaningZh: 因別人之間的衝突而受到波及。
brief.grammar: get/be caught in the crossfire (between/of ...); caught remains the past participle.
brief.register: Vivid idiom, neutral to informal; use sensitively around real violence.
brief.boundaryZh: 比喻義重點是被他人的衝突波及，不是自己主動爭吵，也不只限於實際交火。
brief.misconceptionZh: 沒有參與爭論仍可能受影響；不能把所有工作困難都叫 crossfire。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出第三方如何受到別人爭執的影響。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Junior staff should not get caught in the crossfire of a dispute.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 12, table 2, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The assistants got caught in the crossfire when two departments blamed each other and sent them conflicting instructions.
listening.zh: 兩個部門互相指責，又給助手們互相矛盾的指示，令助手們無辜受到波及。

options.en: They started the dispute deliberately.
options.zh: 他們故意挑起爭執。

options.en: They were affected by a dispute between other people.
options.zh: 他們受到別人之間的爭執影響。

options.en: They resolved the dispute.
options.zh: 他們解決了爭執。

options.en: They independently chose to ignore all instructions.
options.zh: 他們自行決定不理會所有指示。

listening.explanationZh: 衝突來自兩個部門，助手卻收到矛盾指示，正是第三方被波及。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你沒有跟任何人爭吵，為甚麼也受到責怪？
reply.promptEn: Why were you blamed when you were not arguing with anyone?

options.en: I was passing messages between the two sides.
options.zh: 我當時替雙方傳話。

options.en: Their disagreement affected the people helping them.
options.zh: 他們的分歧影響了幫忙的人。

options.en: I got caught in the crossfire of their argument.
options.zh: 我無辜捲入了他們的爭執。

options.en: They directed their frustration at me as well.
options.zh: 他們也把不滿發洩在我身上。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都可解釋未參與爭吵仍被責怪；金句強調第三方受到波及。

scene.promptZh: 兩名活動負責人爭論預算，卻各自要求義工按不同方案採購，義工無論照哪個方案都被責怪。哪句最合適？

options.en: The volunteers got caught in the crossfire.
options.zh: 義工無辜受到雙方衝突波及。

options.en: The volunteers created the budget dispute.
options.zh: 義工挑起了預算爭議。

options.en: The volunteers reached a compromise.
options.zh: 義工達成了折衷方案。

scene.explanationZh: 義工不是爭議的發起人，卻承受互相矛盾的要求與責怪。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 get caught in the crossfire 的比喻義？

options.en: An assistant is blamed during a dispute between her supervisors.
options.zh: 助手在兩名主管的爭執中受到責怪。

options.en: A student chooses to argue directly with a classmate about their own disagreement.
options.zh: 學生主動就自己與同學的分歧直接爭論。

options.en: Children miss an event because adults cannot resolve their argument.
options.zh: 大人無法解決爭執，令孩子錯過活動。

contrast.explanationZh: 第二個情況是直接參與自己的爭議，不是受到其他人衝突波及的第三方。

dialogue.promptZh: 義工說：「兩名負責人都叫我別聽另一位，我根本不知道怎麼做。」哪句最合適？

options.en: You are getting caught in the crossfire. Ask them to agree on one set of instructions.
options.zh: 你正受到他們衝突波及。請他們先統一指示。

options.en: You must have started the argument, so choose a side now.
options.zh: 一定是你挑起爭執，所以現在選一邊吧。

options.en: Try to follow both sets without asking the organisers to clarify.
options.zh: 試着同時跟從兩套指示，不要請主辦者澄清。

dialogue.explanationZh: 辨認第三方受矛盾指示影響，提出先統一指示的辦法；不是責怪義工，也不是要求不澄清便同時照做。

speaking.en: I got caught in the crossfire when the two organisers disagreed.
speaking.zh: 兩位主辦者有分歧時，我無辜受到波及。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明別人的分歧如何影響你。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區兩個小組爭論場地安排，接待員接到互相矛盾的通知，還被兩邊責怪。用一至兩句英文描述接待員的處境，並提出下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明她是第三方而受到爭議影響，不要指控她挑起爭執；可建議統一安排。

examples.en: The receptionist got caught in the crossfire. The groups should agree on one clear message.
examples.zh: 接待員無辜受到衝突波及。兩個小組應先同意一個清楚的訊息。

examples.en: She was caught in the crossfire between the groups, so she needs a single confirmed schedule.
examples.zh: 她無辜受到兩個小組的衝突波及，所以需要一份統一而已確認的時間表。

takeaways.en: Junior staff can get caught in the crossfire of a disagreement.
takeaways.zh: 初級員工可能無辜受到分歧波及。

takeaways.en: The receptionist was caught in the crossfire when the organisers disagreed.
takeaways.zh: 主辦者有分歧時，接待員無辜受到波及。

brief.meaningEn: Follow what most people do or think rather than make an independent choice.
brief.meaningZh: 跟隨大多數人的做法或想法，而非獨立作選擇。
brief.grammar: go along with the crowd; past went, participle gone.
brief.register: Neutral to mildly critical; assess the decision process rather than insult people.
brief.boundaryZh: 與多數人選相同答案不一定是盲從；須有受群體影響而跟隨的線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不表示所有群體決定都錯，也不一定涉及實際人群走動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分獨立同意與未經思考跟隨他人。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Going along with the crowd can prevent people from speaking honestly.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 12, table 2, row 7; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: I voted for the expensive venue just to go along with the crowd, although I preferred the cheaper one.
listening.zh: 我其實偏好較便宜的場地，卻只為跟隨大家而投票選昂貴場地。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼這樣投票？

options.en: The cheaper venue was unavailable.
options.zh: 便宜場地已無法使用。

options.en: The speaker independently preferred the expensive venue.
options.zh: 說話者經獨立考慮後偏好昂貴場地。

options.en: The speaker followed the group despite a different preference.
options.zh: 說話者雖有不同偏好，仍跟隨群體。

options.en: The speaker had checked every cost in detail.
options.zh: 說話者已詳細核對每項費用。

listening.explanationZh: although 交代自己的偏好不同，just to 表示主要動機是跟隨群體。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你不喜歡這個方案，為甚麼剛才仍贊成？
reply.promptEn: Why did you agree just now if you do not like the plan?

options.en: I did not want to be the only person disagreeing.
options.zh: 我不想成為唯一反對的人。

options.en: I was going along with the crowd instead of saying what I thought.
options.zh: 我在跟隨大眾，而沒有說出自己的想法。

options.en: I felt pressure to support the majority.
options.zh: 我感到支持多數人的壓力。

options.en: I kept my doubts to myself because everyone else seemed certain.
options.zh: 大家看來都很肯定，所以我沒說出疑慮。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都說明跟從的動機；金句概括跟隨多數而非獨立表態。

scene.promptZh: 同學沒有看候選人的政綱，只因朋友都選甲，就跟着選甲。哪句最準確？

options.en: She went along with the crowd rather than compare the candidates.
options.zh: 她沒有比較候選人，而是跟隨大眾。

options.en: She reached the same choice after independent research.
options.zh: 她獨立研究後得出相同選擇。

options.en: She persuaded every friend to change their vote.
options.zh: 她說服每位朋友改投其他人。

scene.explanationZh: 沒有查資料而直接跟隨朋友，是判斷過程的關鍵。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜直接說是在 go along with the crowd？

options.en: A student hides a different opinion to avoid standing out.
options.zh: 學生為免顯得不同，隱藏了自己的意見。

options.en: A shopper copies friends without considering her own needs.
options.zh: 購物者沒考慮自己需要，便跟朋友買。

options.en: A member compares the evidence independently and happens to agree with the majority.
options.zh: 組員獨立比較證據後，剛好同意多數人。

contrast.explanationZh: 同意多數不等於盲從；第三個情況有獨立判斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「大家都選這個，你也選吧，不用看資料。」哪句最有建設性？

options.en: I don't want to go along with the crowd without understanding the options.
options.zh: 我不想未了解選項便跟隨大眾。

options.en: The majority is always wrong, so I must choose the opposite.
options.zh: 多數人永遠是錯的，所以我必須選相反的。

options.en: Independent thinking means never agreeing with anyone.
options.zh: 獨立思考就是永遠不同意任何人。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要求了解資料，既不盲從，也不為反對而反對。

speaking.en: I went along with the crowd because I was afraid to disagree.
speaking.zh: 我因為害怕提出異議而跟隨大家。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明跟隨大家的原因。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友都報讀同一個課程，你也差點照做，但你其實對另一科更感興趣。用一至兩句英文說明你會怎樣作選擇。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代獨立比較的做法；不用假定朋友的選擇錯，也不需要故意選相反答案。

examples.en: I do not want to go along with the crowd. I will compare the courses and choose what suits my interests.
examples.zh: 我不想跟隨大眾。我會比較課程，選擇適合自己興趣的。

examples.en: Instead of going along with the crowd, I should consider my own goals before I enrol.
examples.zh: 我不應跟隨大眾，而應在報讀前考慮自己的目標。

takeaways.en: Do not go along with the crowd without considering your own reasons.
takeaways.zh: 不要沒考慮自己的理由便跟隨大眾。

takeaways.en: She went along with the crowd because she did not want to stand out.
takeaways.zh: 她因為不想顯得不同，而跟隨了大眾。

brief.meaningEn: An area where someone’s understanding is weak or where they fail to notice an issue.
brief.meaningZh: 一個人理解不足，或未能察覺問題的範疇。
brief.grammar: a blind spot; plural blind spots; often blind spots in our thinking/understanding.
brief.register: Neutral figurative count noun; use constructively rather than as a personal insult.
brief.boundaryZh: 盲點是理解或察覺的不足，不等於所有弱點，也不表示故意隱瞞。
brief.misconceptionZh: 自己很有經驗仍可能有盲點；外界意見可以幫忙發現，但不代表對方每項批評都正確。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述未被察覺的理解不足，並提出尋求回饋的方法。

sources.sentence: An outside reviewer helped us identify our blind spots.

sources.sentence: Trusted friends can point out our blind spots.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Trusted friends can point out our blind spots.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 84, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We understood the equipment but had a blind spot about how first-time visitors would use it.
listening.zh: 我們了解器材，卻沒考慮到初次到訪的人會怎樣使用它。

options.en: They had no knowledge of any equipment.
options.zh: 他們對任何器材都毫無認識。

options.en: Their understanding did not include the needs of new users.
options.zh: 他們的理解沒有涵蓋新使用者的需要。

options.en: They deliberately hid the instructions from visitors.
options.zh: 他們故意向訪客隱藏說明。

options.en: They had already solved every visitor problem.
options.zh: 他們已解決所有訪客問題。

listening.explanationZh: 團隊懂器材，卻沒有考慮新使用者；盲點不是完全無知，也不是故意隱瞞。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：我們已經檢查很多次，為甚麼還要請新人試用？
reply.promptEn: Why ask new people to test it when we have checked it so often?

options.en: They may notice things we take for granted.
options.zh: 他們可能留意到我們視為理所當然的事。

options.en: A fresh perspective can reveal gaps in our understanding.
options.zh: 新角度可以揭示我們理解的缺口。

options.en: We want to see the experience through unfamiliar eyes.
options.zh: 我們想從不熟悉它的人的角度看體驗。

options.en: New users can help us identify our blind spots.
options.zh: 新使用者可以幫我們找出自己的盲點。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋外部試用的價值；金句指出未察覺的問題。

scene.promptZh: 設計者天天用自己的應用程式，沒發現註冊說明令新用戶困惑，直到試用才知道。哪句最合適？

options.en: The test revealed a blind spot in their understanding of new users.
options.zh: 測試揭示他們理解新用戶時的一個盲點。

options.en: The test proved they intentionally confused users.
options.zh: 測試證明他們故意令用戶困惑。

options.en: The test showed that every part of the design was useless.
options.zh: 測試顯示設計每部分都毫無用處。

scene.explanationZh: 未察覺新用戶困難是具體理解盲點；不能推斷惡意或全盤無用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜稱為自己未察覺的 blind spot？

options.en: An expert overlooks how confusing basic terms are to beginners.
options.zh: 專家忽略基本術語對初學者有多難懂。

options.en: A reviewer notices an assumption the writer has never questioned.
options.zh: 審閱者發現作者從未質疑的一個假設。

options.en: A team clearly identifies a known risk and discusses it openly.
options.zh: 團隊清楚指出已知風險，並公開討論。

contrast.explanationZh: 第三個情況已察覺並討論風險，不能單憑有問題便叫未察覺的盲點。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「有經驗的人不會有盲點吧？」哪句最準確？

options.en: Experience helps, but feedback can still reveal blind spots.
options.zh: 經驗有幫助，但回饋仍可揭示盲點。

options.en: Any blind spot means a person knows nothing at all.
options.zh: 有任何盲點就表示一個人完全無知。

options.en: An outside opinion is always right because it is new.
options.zh: 外界意見因為新，就永遠正確。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認專長與理解缺口可以並存，沒有把所有外界意見當作正確。

speaking.en: Honest feedback helped me recognise a blind spot in my planning.
speaking.zh: 坦誠的回饋幫我認清計劃中的一個盲點。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明回饋幫你發現甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的小組以為海報清楚易懂，但新同學看不明白報名步驟。用一至兩句英文說明發現的問題，以及下次怎樣檢查。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出具體未察覺的理解缺口，並提出檢查方法，不要把一個盲點擴大成全部能力不足。

examples.en: The new students revealed a blind spot in our planning. Next time, we should test the instructions with unfamiliar readers.
examples.zh: 新同學揭示我們計劃中的一個盲點。下次我們應請不熟悉內容的讀者測試說明。

examples.en: We had a blind spot about the registration steps, so we will ask for feedback before printing the next poster.
examples.zh: 我們對報名步驟有個未察覺的理解缺口，所以會在印下一張海報前尋求意見。

takeaways.en: Everyone can have blind spots in their understanding.
takeaways.zh: 每個人的理解都可能有盲點。

takeaways.en: A trusted reviewer can help us identify blind spots in our planning.
takeaways.zh: 受信任的審閱者可以幫我們找出計劃中的盲點。

brief.meaningEn: Seriously damage or destroy something; here, a relationship or group.
brief.meaningZh: 嚴重破壞某事物；本課指關係、合作或團體。
brief.grammar: tear something apart; with a pronoun, tear it apart, not tear apart it; past tore, participle torn.
brief.register: Strong vivid phrasal verb; distinguish relationship destruction from severe criticism in other contexts.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課是關係被破壞，不只是分析或批評作品，也不一定是實際撕開物件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一句爭論不保證關係已完結；可用 could 表示風險，不誇大為必然。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述行為對合作關係的嚴重破壞風險。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: They spent months building the partnership, but one angry message could tear it apart.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 12, table 2, row 9; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The team had worked together for years, but repeated accusations were tearing it apart.
listening.zh: 團隊已合作多年，但反覆指控正在破壞它。
listening.promptZh: 指控對團隊造成甚麼影響？

options.en: They were seriously damaging its unity.
options.zh: 它們正在嚴重破壞團隊團結。

options.en: They were helping every member agree more easily.
options.zh: 它們正在幫助每個組員更容易達成一致。

options.en: They were only improving the wording of a report.
options.zh: 它們只是在改善報告的措辭。

options.en: They had proved every member was guilty.
options.zh: 它們已證明每位組員都有錯。

listening.explanationZh: 上下文是多年合作受損，不是校對報告；也沒有證明所有指控真確。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你不想讓猜疑繼續在小組蔓延？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to stop suspicion spreading through the group?

options.en: It is damaging the trust we have built.
options.zh: 它正在破壞我們建立的信任。

options.en: It could tear the group apart if we do not discuss it honestly.
options.zh: 如果我們不坦誠討論，它可能會破壞整個小組。

options.en: People are beginning to turn against one another.
options.zh: 大家開始互相敵視。

options.en: We risk losing the cooperation the project needs.
options.zh: 我們可能失去項目所需的合作。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋擔心的原因；金句強調團結被嚴重破壞的風險。

scene.promptZh: 合辦項目的兩個小組因不實指控而互不信任，合作快要瓦解。哪句最合適？

options.en: The accusations could tear the partnership apart.
options.zh: 那些指控可能破壞合作關係。

options.en: The accusations are merely a careful review of the poster.
options.zh: 那些指控只是在仔細審閱海報。

options.en: The accusations show that trust has grown stronger.
options.zh: 那些指控顯示信任變得更強。

scene.explanationZh: 情境指向合作關係瓦解，不是只批評某份作品。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句最清楚使用本課「破壞關係」的意思，而非嚴厲批評作品？

options.en: The reviewer tore the essay apart in her comments.
options.zh: 審閱者在評語中把文章批評得體無完膚。

options.en: The dispute tore the team apart and ended their cooperation.
options.zh: 爭執破壞了團隊，令合作結束。

options.en: The editor carefully checked the essay for missing references.
options.zh: 編輯仔細檢查文章有沒有遺漏引文來源。

contrast.explanationZh: 爭執令團隊合作結束，對象與結果都是團隊關係；審閱者批評文章則是另一種批評義。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我想把未經證實的猜測發給全組人。」哪句最負責任？

options.en: That could tear the group apart. Check the facts and speak privately first.
options.zh: 那可能破壞整個小組。先查證事實，再私下談談。

options.en: I thought passing the message on would settle the disagreement, even before anyone checked it.
options.zh: 我以為即使還未有人查證，把訊息傳開也能解決分歧。

options.en: I would send it to everyone first so they could respond to the suspicion together.
options.zh: 我會先傳給所有人，讓大家一起回應這個猜測。

dialogue.explanationZh: 指出風險並建議查證與私下溝通，不以維持團結為由禁止提問。

speaking.en: The argument could tear it apart if we stop listening to one another.
speaking.zh: 如果我們不再互相聆聽，爭執可能破壞這個團體。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用代名詞說出爭執對團體的風險。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你參加的社區劇團因誰應獲功勞而互相指責，信任正在下降。用一至兩句英文說明風險，並建議怎樣處理。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指向團結與合作受損，而非只批評作品；提出公平溝通方法，可用 could 表示風險。

examples.en: The dispute could tear the group apart. We should agree on fair ways to recognise everyone’s work.
examples.zh: 爭議可能破壞整個小組。我們應同意用公平方式肯定每個人的工作。

examples.en: Repeated blame is tearing it apart, so the members need an honest discussion about shared credit.
examples.zh: 反覆責怪正在破壞劇團，所以組員需要坦誠討論如何共同獲得肯定。

takeaways.en: Repeated mistrust can tear a team apart.
takeaways.zh: 反覆猜疑可以破壞一個團隊。

takeaways.en: An unverified accusation could tear the group apart.
takeaways.zh: 未經證實的指控可能破壞整個小組。

brief.meaningEn: Something that seems bad at first but later has a beneficial result.
brief.meaningZh: 起初看來不幸，後來卻帶來好結果的事情。
brief.grammar: be/turn out to be a blessing in disguise; singular count phrase with a.
brief.register: Neutral conversational idiom; avoid dismissing someone’s current suffering.
brief.boundaryZh: 需要先有壞事，再有實際好結果；不是保證每件壞事最終都好。
brief.misconceptionZh: 仍可能有損失；好結果不表示原來的痛苦不重要。
brief.outcomeZh: 能回顧事情如何由壞轉好，而不妄作保證。

sources.sentence: The delay proved a blessing in disguise.

listening.en: Missing that bus was a blessing in disguise: I stayed at the station and found the wallet I had lost.
listening.zh: 錯過那班巴士反而因禍得福：我留在車站，找回遺失的錢包。
listening.promptZh: 為甚麼錯過巴士有意外的好結果？

options.en: It gave the speaker time to recover a lost wallet.
options.zh: 它讓說話者有時間找回遺失的錢包。

options.en: It proved that every delay is beneficial.
options.zh: 它證明每次延誤都有好處。

options.en: The speaker had planned to miss the bus from the start.
options.zh: 說話者一開始就打算錯過巴士。

options.en: The wallet was permanently lost because of the delay.
options.zh: 錢包因延誤而永遠遺失。

listening.explanationZh: 先錯過巴士，後找回錢包，具體的後來好結果構成因禍得福。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：課程取消了，你為甚麼後來反而覺得是好事？
reply.promptEn: Why did you later see the course cancellation as a good thing?

options.en: I found another course that suited me better.
options.zh: 我找到另一個更適合自己的課程。

options.en: The cancellation gave me time to discover a better option.
options.zh: 取消讓我有時間發現更好的選擇。

options.en: It turned out to be a blessing in disguise because the new course was more suitable.
options.zh: 這原來是因禍得福，因為新課程更適合我。

options.en: I was disappointed at first, but the alternative worked out well.
options.zh: 我起初很失望，但替代安排後來很順利。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都提供後來的好結果；金句把先壞後好的關係說清楚。

scene.promptZh: 你未能租到原來想要的場地，後來卻找到更便宜、也更方便長者使用的地方。哪句最合適？

options.en: Losing the first venue turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
options.zh: 租不到第一個場地原來是因禍得福。

options.en: The first rejection guarantees that every future plan will succeed.
options.zh: 第一次被拒絕保證未來所有計劃成功。

options.en: The outcome was entirely negative with no benefit.
options.zh: 結果完全負面，沒有任何好處。

scene.explanationZh: 已有具體更好替代場地，才足以回顧為意外的好結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜現在便說是 a blessing in disguise？

options.en: A failed application leads to a more suitable opportunity.
options.zh: 申請失敗後，出現更適合的機會。

options.en: A cancelled booking leads to a safer and cheaper venue.
options.zh: 預訂取消後，找到更安全、更便宜的場地。

options.en: A person has just suffered a loss and no benefit or later outcome is known.
options.zh: 一個人剛遭受損失，尚未知道任何好處或後來結果。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有後來好結果的證據，不應過早替他人把痛苦說成好事。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我原本很失望，但改期讓家人都能出席了。」哪句最自然？

options.en: It sounds as though the delay was a blessing in disguise.
options.zh: 聽來這次延遲反而是因禍得福。

options.en: So you were wrong to feel disappointed at first.
options.zh: 所以你起初感到失望就是錯的。

options.en: Now every future delay is certain to help you.
options.zh: 現在以後每次延誤都一定會幫到你。

dialogue.explanationZh: 根據實際好結果回應，同時不否定原來的情緒。

speaking.en: The cancelled booking turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
speaking.zh: 預訂取消原來是因禍得福。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再回顧這件起初不順利的事情。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你申請的實習沒有取錄你，後來卻找到更適合興趣的義工工作，還學到實用技巧。用一至兩句英文回顧結果。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出先失望後有益的兩階段，並用具體結果支持；不用聲稱原來的失望沒有道理。

examples.en: The rejection was a blessing in disguise. I found a volunteer role that matched my interests and taught me useful skills.
examples.zh: 被拒絕反而因禍得福。我找到符合興趣的義工工作，也學到實用技巧。

examples.en: Missing the internship turned out to be a blessing in disguise because the alternative helped me discover what I enjoy.
examples.zh: 錯過實習原來是因禍得福，因為替代機會讓我發現自己喜歡做甚麼。

takeaways.en: The delay was a blessing in disguise because it gave us time to improve the plan.
takeaways.zh: 延遲反而因禍得福，因為它讓我們有時間改善計劃。

takeaways.en: Losing that opportunity turned out to be a blessing in disguise when I found a better fit.
takeaways.zh: 當我找到更適合的機會，失去原來機會便成了因禍得福。

brief.meaningEn: An important cause or source of motivation behind an activity or change.
brief.meaningZh: 推動活動或改變的重要原因或動力。
brief.grammar: a driving force behind/in something; one of the driving forces for plural causes.
brief.register: Neutral written and spoken metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 可以是人、動機或因素，不一定是唯一原因，也不要求職位最高。
brief.misconceptionZh: driving 在這裏不是駕車；參與者不一定就是主要推動力量。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出促成行動的關鍵動力，並用實際貢獻支持。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Her determination became a driving force behind the project.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 13, table 1, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Parents’ concerns were a driving force behind the campaign for a safer crossing.
listening.zh: 家長的憂慮是推動爭取更安全過路設施的運動的重要力量。
listening.promptZh: 家長的憂慮有甚麼作用？

options.en: They were a minor issue unrelated to the campaign.
options.zh: 它們是與運動無關的小事。

options.en: They guaranteed the campaign would succeed.
options.zh: 它們保證運動成功。

options.en: They helped motivate and advance the campaign.
options.zh: 它們有助推動和促進運動。

options.en: They were the campaign’s only possible cause.
options.zh: 它們是運動唯一可能的原因。

listening.explanationZh: a driving force 表示重要動力，沒有說是唯一原因或保證成功。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼這個回收計劃一直有人推動？
reply.promptEn: Why does the recycling project keep moving forward?

options.en: Residents care about reducing waste.
options.zh: 居民關心減少廢物。

options.en: Concern for the neighbourhood is a driving force behind it.
options.zh: 對社區的關心是推動它的重要力量。

options.en: A committed group keeps finding ways to improve it.
options.zh: 一群投入的居民不斷找方法改善。

options.en: People can see the practical benefits and want to continue.
options.zh: 大家看見實際好處，想繼續下去。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都提供持續推動的理由；金句明示關鍵動力。

scene.promptZh: 一名居民不斷聯絡街坊、組織會議，令閒置花園終於開始修復。哪句最有根據？

options.en: She was a driving force behind the garden project.
options.zh: 她是推動花園項目的重要力量。

options.en: She attended once as a visitor but did not help organise the project.
options.zh: 她只以訪客身分出席過一次，沒有協助籌辦項目。

options.en: Her effort guarantees the garden will never face another problem.
options.zh: 她的努力保證花園永遠不會再有問題。

scene.explanationZh: 持續聯絡街坊及組織會議支持她是重要推動者，不是只出席一次；仍不保證未來毫無問題。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個人最不宜只憑這些資料稱為 a driving force？

options.en: A volunteer who recruits helpers and keeps the project running.
options.zh: 招募幫手並讓項目持續運作的義工。

options.en: A founder who secures support and organises each stage.
options.zh: 爭取支援並組織每個階段的創辦人。

options.en: A silent one-time visitor, with no other input shown.
options.zh: 只安靜來過一次、未見其他參與的訪客。

contrast.explanationZh: 單次出席不足以證明是重要推動力量；不是否定訪客可能有價值。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「她不是主席，怎會是推動力量？」哪句最準確？

options.en: She can be a driving force through her ideas and effort without holding the top role.
options.zh: 她即使不是最高負責人，也可透過想法和努力成為重要推動力量。

options.en: Only the chairperson can influence a project.
options.zh: 只有主席可以影響項目。

options.en: Anyone who attends once is automatically the main cause.
options.zh: 任何出席過一次的人都自動成為主要原因。

dialogue.explanationZh: 影響來自實際貢獻，不單靠職銜，也不是出席便足夠。

speaking.en: Curiosity was a driving force behind my decision to study science.
speaking.zh: 好奇心是推動我決定修讀科學的重要力量。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明決定背後的重要動力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的同學為了讓新生融入學校，主動招募義工及安排迎新活動，令計劃逐步成形。用一至兩句英文描述她的作用。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用具體組織、動機或行動支持她的重要作用，不要只憑職位或出席下結論。

examples.en: She was a driving force behind the welcome programme. She recruited volunteers and organised activities for new students.
examples.zh: 她是推動迎新計劃的重要力量。她招募義工，也為新生安排活動。

examples.en: Her concern for new students became a driving force, helping the team turn ideas into action.
examples.zh: 她對新生的關心成為重要動力，幫助團隊把想法化成行動。

takeaways.en: Shared curiosity can be a driving force behind a research project.
takeaways.zh: 共同的好奇心可以成為推動研究項目的重要力量。

takeaways.en: She became a driving force by turning the team’s ideas into practical steps.
takeaways.zh: 她把團隊想法化成實際步驟，成為重要推動力量。

brief.meaningEn: Create division or damage a relationship between people.
brief.meaningZh: 令彼此產生隔閡，損害關係。
brief.grammar: drive a wedge between + two people/groups; drove, driven.
brief.register: Vivid idiom; do not assume deliberate intent unless stated.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是關係受到分化，不是任何意見不同；行為可能無意造成。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不一定有人刻意挑撥，也不代表關係永遠無法修補。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明某件事如何削弱彼此的信任或合作。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A dispute over credit can drive a wedge between people who usually cooperate.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 13, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The rumour drove a wedge between us, even though neither of us knew whether it was true.
listening.zh: 謠言令我們產生隔閡，儘管我們誰也不知道它是否屬實。
listening.promptZh: 謠言的主要影響是甚麼？

options.en: It created distance and mistrust between them.
options.zh: 它令他們疏遠並互不信任。

options.en: It confirmed the truth of every accusation.
options.zh: 它證實了每項指控。

options.en: It resolved their dispute.
options.zh: 它解決了他們的爭執。

options.en: It proved both people intended to end the friendship.
options.zh: 它證明兩人都想結束友誼。

listening.explanationZh: 產生隔閡不表示謠言屬實，也不能推斷雙方意圖。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你想先查清楚那個傳言？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to check that rumour first?

options.en: I do not want an unverified story to damage our trust.
options.zh: 我不想讓未經證實的說法破壞信任。

options.en: It could drive a wedge between us if we react without checking.
options.zh: 如果未查證便作反應，它可能令我們產生隔閡。

options.en: We might turn against each other over something false.
options.zh: 我們可能因假的事情而互相敵視。

options.en: Our friendship matters more than a careless assumption.
options.zh: 我們的友誼比草率猜測更重要。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都合理說明查證的原因；金句指出關係分化的風險。

scene.promptZh: 組長只把重要消息告訴部分組員，其他人覺得被排斥，彼此開始不信任。哪句最合適？

options.en: The unequal communication drove a wedge between the members.
options.zh: 不平等的溝通令組員產生隔閡。

options.en: The members had different ideas but continued to share information and trust one another.
options.zh: 組員有不同想法，但仍持續分享資訊並互相信任。

options.en: The arrangement strengthened everyone’s trust equally.
options.zh: 這個安排同樣加強了每個人的信任。

scene.explanationZh: 被排斥及不信任是關係受損的證據；不是仍保持共享資訊與信任，也不是人人更有信任。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 drive a wedge between people？

options.en: A rumour makes friends suspicious of each other.
options.zh: 謠言令朋友互相猜疑。

options.en: Unfair treatment divides a team into hostile groups.
options.zh: 不公平對待令團隊分成敵對陣營。

options.en: Friends discuss different tastes openly and remain close.
options.zh: 朋友坦誠談不同喜好，仍保持親密。

contrast.explanationZh: 有不同喜好而關係未受損，不構成產生隔閡。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我們對設計看法不同，是不是友誼一定完了？」哪句最合適？

options.en: A difference of opinion need not drive a wedge between us if we talk respectfully.
options.zh: 如果互相尊重地討論，意見不同不一定會令我們產生隔閡。

options.en: Any disagreement proves that friendship is impossible.
options.zh: 任何分歧都證明友誼不可能存在。

options.en: We can only stay friends by never expressing different views.
options.zh: 只有永遠不表達不同意見，我們才能做朋友。

dialogue.explanationZh: 區分分歧與關係受損，提出尊重溝通的條件。

speaking.en: Unequal treatment can drive a wedge between people who used to cooperate.
speaking.zh: 不平等對待可能令原本合作的人產生隔閡。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述不平等對待對關係的影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：兩名朋友合辦義賣，一人只公開稱讚自己，另一人因此覺得被忽略，關係變差。用一至兩句英文說明影響及修補方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 連結具體行為與關係變差，提出修補方式；不要直接假定有人故意挑撥。

examples.en: The unfair praise drove a wedge between them. They should acknowledge each other’s contributions.
examples.zh: 不公平的稱讚令他們產生隔閡。他們應肯定彼此的貢獻。

examples.en: Ignoring a friend’s effort can drive a wedge between people, so an honest conversation about shared credit would help.
examples.zh: 忽視朋友的努力會令人產生隔閡，所以坦誠談談如何共同獲得肯定會有幫助。

takeaways.en: A misunderstanding can drive a wedge between friends.
takeaways.zh: 誤會可能令朋友產生隔閡。

takeaways.en: We should not let unverified claims drive a wedge between us.
takeaways.zh: 我們不應讓未經證實的說法令彼此產生隔閡。

titleEn: the glue that holds the group together

target.pattern: (?:\bthe glue that holds the (?:group|team) together\b)|(?:\b(?:act|acts|acted|acting) like glue\b)

brief.meaningEn: The person or factor that keeps a group connected and functioning together.
brief.meaningZh: 讓團體保持連繫、團結與合作的人或因素。
brief.grammar: X is the glue that holds a group together; X can also act like glue, helping family or team members stay connected. The glue is metaphorical.
brief.register: Positive, vivid metaphor for cohesion.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只是單項任務表現好，而是有維繫合作的作用；可指信任、習慣或人。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是一個人必須包辦所有事情；有凝聚作用也不保證沒有分歧。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體合作行為說明團體的凝聚力量。

listening.en: Our weekly check-in is the glue that holds the group together, because it keeps everyone informed and connected.
listening.zh: 每星期的交流是維繫小組的凝聚力量，因為它讓大家了解近況並保持連繫。
listening.promptZh: 每星期的交流為甚麼重要？

options.en: It replaces every member’s individual work.
options.zh: 它取代了每位組員的個人工作。

options.en: It helps the group stay connected and coordinated.
options.zh: 它幫助小組保持連繫和協調。

options.en: It guarantees that the group never disagrees.
options.zh: 它保證小組永遠沒有分歧。

options.en: It is useful only for the strongest member.
options.zh: 它只對能力最強的組員有用。

listening.explanationZh: keeps everyone informed and connected 直接解釋凝聚作用，不表示取代工作或消除所有分歧。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你們即使很忙，也保留每週交流？
reply.promptEn: Why keep the weekly check-in even when everyone is busy?

options.en: It keeps everyone aware of what others are doing.
options.zh: 它讓大家知道其他人在做甚麼。

options.en: It gives us a regular chance to support one another.
options.zh: 它給我們定期互相支援的機會。

options.en: It is the glue that holds the group together.
options.zh: 它是維繫小組的凝聚力量。

options.en: Without it, we would lose an important connection.
options.zh: 沒有它，我們會失去一項重要連繫。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋交流的維繫作用；金句用黏合的比喻。

scene.promptZh: 遠距離工作的成員靠坦誠交流與互信持續合作，即使很少見面也願意互相幫忙。哪句最準確？

options.en: Trust is the glue that holds the team together.
options.zh: 信任是維繫團隊的凝聚力量。

options.en: Trust means they no longer need any communication.
options.zh: 信任表示他們再也不需要溝通。

options.en: Distance kept them from working together.
options.zh: 距離令他們無法合作。

scene.explanationZh: 互信讓分散成員保持合作，正是維繫作用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個因素最不宜稱為 the glue that holds the group together？

options.en: A shared habit of listening and offering help.
options.zh: 共同聆聽並提供幫忙的習慣。

options.en: A trusted member who keeps communication open.
options.zh: 讓溝通保持暢通、受信任的組員。

options.en: A rule that isolates members and prevents them sharing information.
options.zh: 令組員彼此孤立、不能分享資訊的規則。

contrast.explanationZh: 阻止連繫及分享的規則與凝聚作用相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 組員說：「她像小組的黏合劑，所以所有工作都該交她做。」哪句最公平？

options.en: She may be the glue that holds the group together, but we must still share the work.
options.zh: 她可能是維繫小組的凝聚力量，但我們仍必須分擔工作。

options.en: Keeping a group connected means doing every task alone.
options.zh: 維繫小組就表示一個人獨自做全部工作。

options.en: If she is helpful, nobody else needs to contribute.
options.zh: 如果她樂於幫忙，其他人就不必貢獻。

dialogue.explanationZh: 凝聚作用不等於包辦一切，仍須公平分工。

speaking.en: Shared trust is the glue that holds the group together.
speaking.zh: 共同的信任是維繫小組的凝聚力量。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明甚麼因素維繫團體。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：畢業後朋友住在不同地區，但每月固定視像聊天，分享近況及互相鼓勵，因此仍然親密。用一至兩句英文描述這個習慣的作用。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用保持連繫或互相支援說明凝聚作用，不要把一個人或習慣寫成取代所有人的責任。

examples.en: Our monthly call is the glue that holds the group together. It helps us share news and support one another.
examples.zh: 每月的通話是維繫我們的凝聚力量。它讓我們分享近況，互相支持。

examples.en: Regular conversations are the glue that holds the group together, even though we now live far apart.
examples.zh: 雖然我們現在住得很遠，定期談話仍是維繫我們的凝聚力量。

takeaways.en: Honest communication is the glue that holds the team together.
takeaways.zh: 坦誠溝通是維繫團隊的凝聚力量。

takeaways.en: A trusted coordinator can act like glue when two volunteer teams need to cooperate.
takeaways.zh: 兩支義工隊需要合作時，一位受信任的統籌者可以發揮凝聚作用。

target.pattern: \ba (?:(?:meaningful|limited|key) )?(?:part|role) to play\b|\ban important (?:part|role) to play\b|\bplay(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:a (?:(?:meaningful|limited|key) )?|an important )(?:part|role)\b|\bplay(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) part\b

brief.meaningEn: Have a role or contribution to make; meaningful adds value, important/key emphasise importance, while limited restricts extent.
brief.meaningZh: 有可擔任的角色或可作出的貢獻；meaningful 加上價值，important/key 強調重要，limited 則限制作用大小。
brief.grammar: have a (meaningful/limited/key) part/role to play in + noun/-ing; have an important part/role to play; also play a (meaningful/limited/key) part/role or play an important part/role. The adjective changes degree or evaluation, not the core contribution frame. Play one’s part gives the contribution a possessive frame, often the contribution expected in a shared effort; the scope still needs context.
brief.register: Encouraging neutral English; not necessarily a theatrical role.
brief.boundaryZh: 角色可以小而有價值，不必掌握領導權；但要有實質作用，不只是掛名。 meaningful 評價有價值，limited 限制作用大小；範圍小不等於沒有作用，也不必同時稱為重要。 important/key 表示重要作用，仍不等於唯一原因或保證成果。 play one’s part 可強調在共同努力中應作的貢獻，不代表各人需做相同事情。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是保證每人做同樣的事，也不是沒有經驗便不能貢獻。
brief.outcomeZh: 能為不同成員指出有價值的參與角色。

listening.en: Even the youngest volunteers have a meaningful part to play in welcoming visitors and explaining the displays.
listening.zh: 即使最年輕的義工，也能透過接待訪客和介紹展品作出有價值的貢獻。
listening.promptZh: 說話者對年輕義工有甚麼看法？

options.en: They must lead every activity before their work matters.
options.zh: 他們必須帶領所有活動，工作才有意義。

options.en: They can only observe and should not contribute.
options.zh: 他們只能觀察，不應貢獻。

options.en: They have useful responsibilities despite their age.
options.zh: 雖然年紀小，他們仍有有用的責任。

options.en: They can contribute only after becoming experienced leaders.
options.zh: 他們必須成為有經驗的領袖後才能貢獻。

listening.explanationZh: 接待與介紹展品是具體貢獻，不要求年輕人當領袖。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：我是新組員，也可以幫得上忙嗎？
reply.promptEn: Can I really help when I am new to the group?

options.en: You can help test the instructions from a newcomer’s point of view.
options.zh: 你可以從新人的角度幫忙測試說明。

options.en: You have a meaningful part to play in making the project welcoming.
options.zh: 你可以在令項目更親切易用方面作出有價值的貢獻。

options.en: Your questions can show us what needs to be clearer.
options.zh: 你的問題能讓我們知道哪些地方需要更清楚。

options.en: We need your fresh perspective as well as experienced members’ skills.
options.zh: 我們既需要有經驗組員的技巧，也需要你的新角度。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都指出新人實際可作的貢獻；金句不只是空泛稱讚。

scene.promptZh: 新組員不熟悉設計軟件，卻能請新生試用並整理意見，幫助改善作品。哪句最合適？

options.en: She has a meaningful part to play in improving the design.
options.zh: 她可以在改善設計方面作出有價值的貢獻。

options.en: Her work has no value because she cannot use the software.
options.zh: 因為不會用軟件，她的工作毫無價值。

options.en: She must replace the designer for her contribution to matter.
options.zh: 她必須取代設計者，貢獻才有價值。

scene.explanationZh: 整理真實使用者意見能改善作品，是不同但有用的角色。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個安排最不符合讓人有 a meaningful part to play？

options.en: Give a new member a real testing task and discuss their findings.
options.zh: 給新組員實際測試任務，並討論結果。

options.en: Assign someone a title but never let them do anything or influence the work.
options.zh: 只給某人職銜，從不讓他做事或影響工作。

options.en: Ask a quiet member to research a topic the group needs.
options.zh: 請安靜的組員研究小組需要的題目。

contrast.explanationZh: 只有掛名而沒有實際作用，不能算有意義的貢獻角色。

dialogue.promptZh: 組員說：「我不是組長，所以做甚麼都不重要。」哪句最能回應？

options.en: You have a meaningful part to play in checking facts; the whole team relies on accurate information.
options.zh: 你可以在核對資料方面作出重要貢獻；整個團隊都需要準確資訊。

options.en: Only a leader can make any contribution.
options.zh: 只有領袖才能作出任何貢獻。

options.en: Your title matters more than whether the work helps.
options.zh: 你的職銜比工作是否有幫助更重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 指出具體任務與作用，讓貢獻的價值有根據。

speaking.en: Every member has a meaningful part to play in keeping the community garden running.
speaking.zh: 每位組員都可以為維持社區花園運作作出有價值的貢獻。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明每位組員的參與價值。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一名不擅長上台的同學認為自己不能幫忙校慶，但他很細心，可負責核對訪客名單和接待安排。用一至兩句英文鼓勵他。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出具體而有作用的任務，鼓勵時不要只給空泛稱讚，也不要求他做不適合的角色。

examples.en: You have a meaningful part to play in checking the guest list. Your careful work will help the event run smoothly.
examples.zh: 你可以在核對嘉賓名單方面作出有價值的貢獻。你的細心工作會令活動更順利。

examples.en: You have a meaningful part to play even without going on stage, because accurate reception plans matter.
examples.zh: 即使不上台，你仍可以作出有價值的貢獻，因為準確的接待安排很重要。

takeaways.en: New members have a meaningful part to play in testing our ideas.
takeaways.zh: 新組員可以在測試想法方面作出有價值的貢獻。

takeaways.en: You have a meaningful part to play even when your role is behind the scenes.
takeaways.zh: 即使是幕後角色，你仍可以作出有價值的貢獻。

brief.meaningEn: Depend on each other for help or support.
brief.meaningZh: 彼此依靠，互相提供幫助或支援。
brief.grammar: rely on + person; one another makes the dependence reciprocal; relies, relied, relying.
brief.register: Neutral everyday English; multiword verb with on.
brief.boundaryZh: 是互相依靠，不是單向要求對方包辦，也不代表失去獨立能力。
brief.misconceptionZh: 支援可以不完全相同；互相依靠不保證每個人任何時候都能幫忙。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述團體互惠支援及合理界線。

listening.en: We rely on one another: I help with transport, and my neighbour checks on my cat when I travel.
listening.zh: 我們互相依靠：我幫忙交通接送，鄰居則在我外遊時照顧我的貓。

options.en: Only the speaker receives help and never contributes.
options.zh: 只有說話者接受幫助，從不貢獻。

options.en: Both people provide different kinds of support.
options.zh: 兩人提供不同形式的互相支援。

options.en: They must provide exactly the same service.
options.zh: 他們必須提供完全相同的服務。

options.en: One person does both jobs without help.
options.zh: 一人沒有協助地完成兩項工作。

listening.explanationZh: 接送與照顧貓是不同但互惠的幫忙，不要求完全相同。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你們住在同一條街，遇到小問題怎樣處理？
reply.promptEn: How do you handle small problems when you live on the same street?

options.en: We ask neighbours for help and return the favour when we can.
options.zh: 我們會請鄰居幫忙，也在可以時回報。

options.en: We share small tasks according to our skills.
options.zh: 我們按各自的能力分擔小任務。

options.en: We rely on one another for practical support.
options.zh: 我們互相依靠，提供實際支援。

options.en: Someone usually knows how to help, and we take turns contributing.
options.zh: 通常有人知道怎樣幫忙，我們輪流出力。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都描述互惠支援；金句沒有說失去獨立能力。

scene.promptZh: 兩個朋友一人擅長校對，一人擅長排版，互相檢查對方的作業，也願意幫忙。哪句最合適？

options.en: They rely on one another while contributing different skills.
options.zh: 他們互相依靠，同時提供不同技巧。

options.en: One does all the work while the other refuses to help.
options.zh: 一人做全部工作，另一人拒絕幫忙。

options.en: They cannot contribute unless their skills are identical.
options.zh: 除非技巧相同，否則他們無法貢獻。

scene.explanationZh: 不同技巧可以形成互惠支援，不要求任務相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 rely on one another？

options.en: Two neighbours exchange practical help when they can.
options.zh: 兩名鄰居在可以時互相提供實際幫助。

options.en: Team members share information and cover agreed tasks.
options.zh: 組員分享資訊，協助處理約定任務。

options.en: One person demands constant help but refuses every request from the other.
options.zh: 一人要求對方不斷幫忙，卻拒絕對方所有請求。

contrast.explanationZh: 第三個情況是單向依賴，不是互相依靠。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「互相依靠就表示你必須隨時幫我吧？」哪句最合適？

options.en: We can rely on one another while respecting each other’s time and limits.
options.zh: 我們可以互相依靠，同時尊重彼此的時間和界線。

options.en: Mutual support means one person must always be available.
options.zh: 互相支持就是一人必須隨時候命。

options.en: If you ever say no, we have never supported each other.
options.zh: 只要你曾拒絕，就表示我們從未互相支持。

dialogue.explanationZh: 互惠不等於無限責任，保留合理界線仍可互相幫忙。

speaking.en: We rely on one another, but we also respect each other’s limits.
speaking.zh: 我們互相依靠，但也尊重彼此的界線。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再同時說明支援與界線。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與朋友合辦讀書會，你整理題目，他聯絡參加者；遇到困難時會互相幫忙。用一至兩句英文描述合作。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出雙方的貢獻與互惠支援，不要把它寫成其中一人包辦全部工作。

examples.en: We rely on one another to run the reading group. I prepare questions, and he contacts the participants.
examples.zh: 我們互相依靠來營運讀書會。我準備問題，他聯絡參加者。

examples.en: We rely on one another when problems arise, while each of us takes responsibility for a different task.
examples.zh: 遇到問題時，我們互相依靠，同時各自負責不同任務。

takeaways.en: Good neighbours can rely on one another for practical help.
takeaways.zh: 好鄰居可以互相依靠，提供實際幫助。

takeaways.en: We rely on one another without expecting unlimited availability.
takeaways.zh: 我們互相依靠，但不期待對方隨時候命。

target.pattern: (?:\b(?:get|gets|getting|got|gotten) on the same wavelength\b)|(?:\b(?:am|are|is|was|were|be|been|being) on the same wavelength\b)

brief.meaningEn: Begin to understand one another and think in a compatible way.
brief.meaningZh: 開始理解彼此，想法能互相配合。
brief.grammar: get on the same wavelength marks reaching mutual understanding; be on the same wavelength describes an existing shared way of thinking. Use a suitable form of be or get.
brief.register: Neutral to informal communication idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 不要求每個細節都同意，而是能理解彼此的意思、目標或做法。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不用真的談無線電，也不表示永遠沒有分歧；get 強調逐漸達到共通理解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述澄清目標後改善理解與協調。

titleEn: in the spotlight / in the public eye

brief.meaningEn: Receiving a lot of public attention; in the public eye often describes a person who is widely visible in media.
brief.meaningZh: 受到大量公眾注意；in the public eye 常形容人物在媒體上廣為人知。
brief.grammar: Be/put someone in the spotlight; be/remain in the public eye. Both phrases refer to public attention, and neither fixes how long it lasts.
brief.register: Neutral media language; a journalist explains public visibility and interview boundaries to a colleague.
brief.boundaryZh: 兩個片語都可指公開受注目；不能只以時間長短區分，也不保證當事人喜歡受訪。
brief.misconceptionZh: 公眾注意不等於讚賞、完全公開私生活或願意接受每次訪問。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述人物受到廣泛公眾注意，並把曝光與本人意願分開。

brief.meaningEn: Become established and begin to be accepted or develop.

brief.grammar: take root; took root, has taken root; often an idea, belief, practice or habit as subject. The habit remains the subject of take root, rather than a direct object of plant.
brief.register: Conventional plant metaphor in neutral English.

options.en: People now expect one another to check the source.

options.en: The group has gradually made checking part of its routine.
options.zh: 小組逐漸把核對變成日常流程的一部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都說明習慣建立；金句以扎根比喻穩定發展。

scene.promptZh: 小組起初只試行每週回顧，幾個月後大家會主動準備，甚至不用提醒。哪句最準確？

options.en: The practice has taken root in the group.
options.zh: 這個做法已在小組中扎根建立。

options.en: The practice happened once and disappeared.
options.zh: 這個做法只出現一次便消失。

options.en: The practice can never change again.
options.zh: 這個做法永遠不能再改變。

scene.explanationZh: 持續數月並主動採用，顯示已成為穩定做法；不表示永久不可改。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜說已經 taken root？

options.en: A helpful routine becomes normal after months of use.
options.zh: 有用的流程經過幾個月使用後成為常態。

options.en: A belief spreads and becomes widely accepted.
options.zh: 一種信念流傳並廣泛得到接受。

options.en: A rule is mentioned once, ignored by everyone and never used again.
options.zh: 規則只被提過一次，大家不理會，以後也沒使用。

contrast.explanationZh: 單次提及而未被採用，不等於建立。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「我們今天試了新習慣一次，是不是已經扎根了？」哪句最準確？

options.en: It may take time for the habit to take root; we need to use it regularly.
options.zh: 習慣可能需要時間才會扎根；我們要經常運用。

options.en: Treat one trial as a settled habit.
options.zh: 把一次試行當作已穩定建立的習慣。

options.en: Only a good habit can take root; harmful ideas cannot.
options.zh: 只有好習慣可以扎根；有害想法不可以。

dialogue.explanationZh: 一次試行不足以顯示習慣已穩定建立；需要持續採用，而且好壞習慣都可 take root。

speaking.en: The new routine took root after we used it for several months.
speaking.zh: 我們使用幾個月後，新流程逐漸建立起來。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述流程如何逐漸扎根。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的班別開始每天整理課室，幾個月後同學不需提醒也會自動做。用一至兩句英文描述習慣的發展。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用持續採用與不用提醒等線索支持建立，不要把一次嘗試當成穩定習慣。

examples.en: The habit of tidying the classroom has taken root. Students now do it without reminders.
examples.zh: 整理課室的習慣已扎根建立。學生現在不用提醒也會做。

examples.en: Daily tidying took root through regular practice and shared responsibility.
examples.zh: 每天整理的習慣透過持續實行及共同責任而逐漸建立。

takeaways.en: A useful routine can take root through repeated practice.
takeaways.zh: 有用的流程可以透過反覆實行而逐漸建立。

takeaways.en: The idea took root when people saw it working in daily life.
takeaways.zh: 當大家看見它在日常生活中有效，這個想法便逐漸扎根。

brief.meaningEn: During the course of a process or journey.
brief.meaningZh: 在一段過程或旅程之中。
brief.grammar: along the way is an adverbial phrase; often at sentence end.
brief.register: Neutral conventional phrase; literal journey and figurative process are both common.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只指最後結果，也不必從開始至結束每一刻都發生。
brief.misconceptionZh: 學習途中的困難或收穫都可用，不等於必須走在實際道路上。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把過程中的收穫或問題與最終結果區分。

listening.en: We did not win the contest, but we learned to organise our work along the way.
listening.zh: 我們沒有贏得比賽，但在過程中學會了安排工作。

options.en: Winning was the only result that mattered.
options.zh: 獲勝是唯一重要結果。

options.en: Useful learning happened during the process of taking part.
options.zh: 參與過程中發生了有用的學習。

options.en: The team learned the skill only after all work had ended.
options.zh: 團隊只在所有工作結束後才學會技巧。

options.en: The team never encountered any difficulty.
options.zh: 團隊從沒遇到困難。

listening.explanationZh: along the way 指參與整個過程中的學習，不只準備階段，也不只看最終勝負。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：雖然計劃最後改變了，你有甚麼收穫？
reply.promptEn: What did you gain even though the plan changed in the end?

options.en: We learned a lot along the way about listening to users.
options.zh: 我們在過程中學到很多聆聽使用者的方法。

options.en: The discussions helped us understand what people needed.
options.zh: 討論幫我們理解大家的需要。

options.en: I became better at asking useful questions during the project.
options.zh: 項目進行期間，我更懂得問有用的問題。

options.en: Trying different approaches taught us what worked.
options.zh: 嘗試不同方法讓我們知道甚麼有效。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都談過程中的收穫；金句不用把原定結果成功作前提。

scene.promptZh: 學生做研究時多次修改方法，途中發現原來沒想過的新問題。哪句最合適？

options.en: They made useful discoveries along the way.
options.zh: 他們在過程中有了有用的發現。

options.en: Nothing happened until the final result appeared.
options.zh: 最終結果出現前，甚麼也沒發生。

options.en: They kept the original method unchanged throughout the research.
options.zh: 他們整個研究過程都維持原來方法，沒有改動。

scene.explanationZh: 研究進行中修改方法並有新發現，符合過程義；不是等到最後才發生一切，也不是方法全程不變。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 along the way？

options.en: Something happens during the process.
options.zh: 某事在過程中發生。

options.en: A lesson can be learned before the final outcome.
options.zh: 最終結果出現前，也可以有所學習。

options.en: Something must happen only at the very end, never during the process.
options.zh: 某事必須只在最終一刻發生，過程中絕不發生。

contrast.explanationZh: along the way 正是途中或過程之中，不能限定為最後一刻。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「沒有拿獎，整個項目便毫無價值。」哪句最有建設性？

options.en: We still developed useful skills along the way. Let's identify what we can use next time.
options.zh: 我們仍在過程中培養了有用技巧。看看下次可以運用甚麼吧。

options.en: A final result is the only possible source of learning.
options.zh: 最終結果是唯一可能的學習來源。

options.en: Learning during the process means the final outcome must have been perfect.
options.zh: 過程中有所學習就表示最終結果一定完美。

dialogue.explanationZh: 指出過程價值，同時不假裝最終結果完美。

speaking.en: We changed the plan several times and learned useful lessons along the way.
speaking.zh: 我們多次修改計劃，也在過程中學到有用的經驗。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述過程中的收穫。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你初次籌辦市集，雖然人流不及預期，但途中學會聯絡攤主和安排時間。用一至兩句英文回顧收穫。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把過程中的學習與最後結果分開；具體說明學到甚麼，不用假裝活動達到原定人流。

examples.en: The market was quieter than expected, but I learned to contact stallholders along the way.
examples.zh: 市集比預期冷清，但我在過程中學會了聯絡攤主。

examples.en: I gained useful planning skills along the way, even though the final turnout was disappointing.
examples.zh: 雖然最後人流令人失望，我仍在過程中獲得有用的策劃技巧。

takeaways.en: We can learn valuable lessons along the way.
takeaways.zh: 我們可以在過程中學到寶貴經驗。

takeaways.en: The project changed, but we discovered better methods along the way.
takeaways.zh: 項目改變了，但我們在過程中發現更好的方法。

brief.meaningEn: Choose channels or places where an audience is already focusing.
brief.meaningZh: 選擇觀眾或受眾已在留意的渠道或地方。
brief.grammar: go where the attention is; a productive metaphorical clause, not a fixed idiom.
brief.register: Informal discussion of communication, outreach or advertising.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定真的搬到某地，也不保證受眾會接受訊息；要看所指受眾及目標。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是只追逐名氣，或認為最熱鬧的地方對每個目標都合適。
brief.outcomeZh: 能根據目標受眾選擇傳遞訊息的渠道。

sources.sentence: Businesses often go where the attention is when choosing ad platforms.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 14, table 2, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: To reach local parents, the organiser went where the attention is and shared the notice in the community chat.
listening.zh: 為了接觸區內家長，主辦者到受眾留意的渠道，在社區聊天群組分享通知。

options.en: They used a channel the intended audience already followed.
options.zh: 他們使用目標受眾本來就在留意的渠道。

options.en: They chose a channel unrelated to local parents.
options.zh: 他們選了與區內家長無關的渠道。

options.en: They guaranteed that every parent would attend.
options.zh: 他們保證每位家長都會出席。

options.en: They stopped considering who the notice was for.
options.zh: 他們不再考慮通知是給誰看的。

listening.explanationZh: 目的為接觸區內家長，渠道是家長留意的社區群組；不保證出席。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼把活動消息放在學生常用的平台？
reply.promptEn: Why post the event on a platform students already use?

options.en: That is where our intended readers already spend time.
options.zh: 目標讀者本來就在那裏花時間。

options.en: We want the notice to reach students who might be interested.
options.zh: 我們想讓可能感興趣的學生看到通知。

options.en: We are trying to go where the attention is rather than wait for people to find us.
options.zh: 我們嘗試到受眾留意的地方，而不是等別人找到我們。

options.en: It makes the message easier for the right audience to notice.
options.zh: 這讓合適的受眾更容易留意訊息。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都以目標受眾解釋渠道選擇；金句是語境中的自然比喻。

scene.promptZh: 中心想讓長者知道新課程，發現他們常看社區通訊，便在那裏刊登消息。哪句最合適？

options.en: The centre chose to go where the attention is for its intended audience.
options.zh: 中心選擇到目標受眾留意的地方傳遞訊息。

options.en: The centre chose the busiest platform without checking who used it.
options.zh: 中心沒有檢查使用者，便選最熱鬧的平台。

options.en: The notice guarantees that every reader will enrol.
options.zh: 通知保證每位讀者都會報讀。

scene.explanationZh: 選擇跟受眾習慣有根據的渠道，而非不分對象追逐人流。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不符合有目的地 go where the attention is？

options.en: Use a community page that target readers regularly follow.
options.zh: 使用目標讀者常看的社區專頁。

options.en: Share a school notice through the channel parents actually read.
options.zh: 透過家長實際閱讀的渠道分享學校通知。

options.en: Choose a famous platform without checking whether the intended audience uses it.
options.zh: 不查目標受眾是否使用，就選一個知名平台。

contrast.explanationZh: 渠道知名不等於目標受眾在留意；需要對象及目的相符。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「這個平台很紅，所以所有宣傳都放這裏吧。」哪句最合適？

options.en: We should go where the attention is for our audience, so let's check who uses it first.
options.zh: 我們應到自己受眾留意的地方，所以先看看誰在使用吧。

options.en: A popular channel guarantees that every campaign succeeds.
options.zh: 熱門渠道保證每個宣傳成功。

options.en: The identity of the audience never matters.
options.zh: 受眾是誰永遠不重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留比喻意思，同時要求查受眾，避免人氣等於適用的錯誤。

speaking.en: We need to go where the attention is if we want local families to notice the event.
speaking.zh: 如果想讓區內家庭留意活動，我們要到受眾留意的地方傳遞訊息。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把渠道選擇連結到目標受眾。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想招募學生參加閱讀活動，發現大家常看學校的每週電子通訊。用一至兩句英文說明你會在哪裏發布，以及原因。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出受眾實際關注的渠道及原因；不要聲稱所有看到通知的人必定參加。

examples.en: We should go where the attention is and use the weekly school newsletter, which students already read.
examples.zh: 我們應到受眾留意的地方，使用學生本來就會讀的每週學校通訊。

examples.en: To reach interested students, we will go where the attention is by sharing the activity in the school newsletter.
examples.zh: 為了接觸有興趣的學生，我們會到受眾留意的地方，在學校通訊分享活動。

takeaways.en: Organisers can go where the attention is while keeping their intended audience in mind.
takeaways.zh: 主辦者可以到受眾留意的地方，同時記住自己的目標對象。

takeaways.en: We went where the attention is by using a channel local parents already trusted.
takeaways.zh: 我們使用區內家長本來信任的渠道，到受眾留意的地方傳遞訊息。

listening.en: While sorting old photographs, I came across a letter I had not seen for years.
listening.zh: 整理舊照片時，我偶然發現一封多年沒見過的信。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣找到那封信？

options.en: By following a search plan specifically for the letter.
options.zh: 按照專門找信的搜尋計劃。

options.en: By encountering it unexpectedly during another activity.
options.zh: 在做另一件事時意外發現它。

options.en: By receiving a new letter from the writer that day.
options.zh: 當天收到作者寄來的新信。

options.en: By deciding that the letter seemed friendly.
options.zh: 判斷那封信給人友善的印象。

listening.explanationZh: 本來整理照片，卻發現舊信，是未預計的發現。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你怎樣找到那個很小的博物館？
reply.promptEn: How did you find that tiny museum?

options.en: I noticed it while exploring a side street.
options.zh: 我在探索小街時留意到它。

options.en: I had not planned to visit it, but the sign caught my eye.
options.zh: 我本來沒打算參觀，但招牌吸引了我。

options.en: I came across it while walking around the neighbourhood.
options.zh: 我在社區散步時偶然遇到它。

options.en: I found it by chance on my way somewhere else.
options.zh: 我去別處途中碰巧發現它。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都描述意外發現；金句不是刻意搜尋。

scene.promptZh: 你查巴士時間時，意外看到一篇介紹附近花園的文章。哪句最準確？

options.en: I came across an article about the garden while checking bus times.
options.zh: 我查巴士時間時，偶然發現一篇介紹花園的文章。

options.en: I searched only for that exact article until I found it.
options.zh: 我一直只找那篇指定文章，直到找到。

options.en: The article came across as impatient.
options.zh: 那篇文章給人不耐煩的印象。

scene.explanationZh: 查巴士時間卻偶然發現花園文章，保留原本目的與意外發現的關係；came across as 則描述給人的印象。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句使用的是「給人印象」，而非本課「偶然遇到」的意思？

options.en: I came across an old notebook in the drawer.
options.zh: 我在抽屜偶然發現一本舊筆記簿。

options.en: She came across as confident during the interview.
options.zh: 她在面試時給人自信的印象。

options.en: We came across a quiet café on our walk.
options.zh: 我們散步時偶然遇到一間安靜的咖啡店。

contrast.explanationZh: come across as 接印象；come across 加人或物則可指偶然遇到。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我偶然看到這個網上說法，所以一定是真的吧？」哪句最合適？

options.en: You may have come across it by chance, but you still need to check the source.
options.zh: 你可能是偶然看到它，但仍要核對來源。

options.en: Since the wording sounds familiar, I would repeat it without looking for its source.
options.zh: 既然字句聽來熟悉，我會不找來源就轉述。

options.en: I thought “come across” meant you had searched specifically for that claim.
options.zh: 我以為 come across 表示你曾特別搜尋這個說法。

dialogue.explanationZh: 發現方式不等於內容可靠，仍需查證。

brief.meaningEn: Extremely quickly, often seeming almost instantaneous.
brief.meaningZh: 非常迅速，快得彷彿轉眼之間。

brief.outcomeZh: 能描述快速變化，並區分速度與準備時間。

scene.promptZh: 活動報名一開始，名額幾乎立刻滿額。哪句最合適？

options.en: The places were filled in the blink of an eye.
options.zh: 名額轉眼之間就滿了。

options.en: The places filled slowly over several months.
options.zh: 名額花了幾個月才慢慢填滿。

options.en: The speed proves that no preparation was needed.
options.zh: 這個速度證明不需任何準備。

scene.explanationZh: 幾乎立刻滿額支持快速比喻，卻不支持沒有準備的推論。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜用 in the blink of an eye 描述其速度？

options.en: A message spreads through the whole group within moments.
options.zh: 訊息片刻間傳遍整個群組。

options.en: All remaining tickets are bought almost immediately.
options.zh: 所有餘票幾乎立即被買走。

options.en: A project progresses slowly through several years of gradual work.
options.zh: 項目經過多年逐步工作才緩慢推進。

contrast.explanationZh: 明確漫長而緩慢的過程與極迅速的意思相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「影片轉眼間成功，拍攝一定不需努力吧？」哪句最準確？

options.en: It spread in the blink of an eye, but producing it took months of work.
options.zh: 它轉眼間流傳開來，但製作花了幾個月努力。

options.en: Fast popularity proves that all the work was easy.
options.zh: 迅速受歡迎就證明全部工作都很容易。

options.en: A quick result means there can have been no preparation.
options.zh: 結果迅速就表示不可能有準備。

dialogue.explanationZh: 區分快速傳播與事前投入，不由結果速度推斷工作容易。

speaking.en: The message spread through our group in the blink of an eye.
speaking.zh: 訊息轉眼間傳遍了我們的小組。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述訊息傳播的速度。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的小組花了一個月製作短片，發布後卻在很短時間內被大量分享。用一至兩句英文對比製作與傳播時間。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把非常快的傳播與較長準備時間區分；不必當作實際眨眼計時。

examples.en: The video spread in the blink of an eye, but we had spent a month producing it.
examples.zh: 影片轉眼間流傳開來，但我們花了一個月製作。

examples.en: After weeks of careful work, our clip reached a huge audience in the blink of an eye.
examples.zh: 經過幾星期仔細製作，我們的短片轉眼間接觸到大量觀眾。

takeaways.en: The news travelled around the school in the blink of an eye.
takeaways.zh: 消息轉眼間傳遍學校。

takeaways.en: The tickets vanished in the blink of an eye despite months of preparation.
takeaways.zh: 雖然籌備花了幾個月，門票卻轉眼間售罄。

brief.meaningEn: In the most prominent position or receiving especially clear attention.
brief.meaningZh: 在最顯著的位置，或受到特別明確的重視。
brief.grammar: put/keep something front and centre; something appears/is front and centre. British centre, American center.
brief.register: Neutral to informal conventional spatial expression; physical display or abstract priorities.
brief.boundaryZh: 可以指版面位置或議題優先程度，不必精確位於幾何中心；顯眼不代表唯一考慮。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是只把東西放在實際中央，也不保證大家接受或喜歡它。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述刻意凸顯的內容或重視的議題。

listening.en: The new guide puts accessibility front and centre, with clear routes and support information on the opening page.
listening.zh: 新指南把無障礙使用放在最顯著位置，在首頁列出清楚路線與支援資訊。
listening.promptZh: 指南怎樣處理無障礙使用？

options.en: It makes it a prominent and clear focus.
options.zh: 它把這點明確凸顯為重點。

options.en: It hides it in an unrelated section.
options.zh: 它把這點藏在無關章節。

options.en: It guarantees every reader has the same needs.
options.zh: 它保證每個讀者都有相同需要。

options.en: It removes all other information from the guide.
options.zh: 它刪掉指南的所有其他資訊。

listening.explanationZh: 首頁清楚列出資料是凸顯的具體做法，不表示刪除所有其他內容。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：新首頁怎樣讓大家留意報名限期？
reply.promptEn: How does the new homepage draw attention to the registration deadline?

options.en: The date appears clearly in the main section.
options.zh: 日期清楚顯示在主要部分。

options.en: We have put the deadline front and centre.
options.zh: 我們把限期放在最顯著位置。

options.en: Readers can see the key date before looking at the details.
options.zh: 讀者看細節前便能看見關鍵日期。

options.en: The layout gives the deadline particular emphasis.
options.zh: 版面特別凸顯限期。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋凸顯方式；金句不要求日期精確位於幾何中心。

scene.promptZh: 社區計劃每次會議先談居民需要，報告首頁也清楚列出。哪句最合適？

options.en: The project keeps residents’ needs front and centre.
options.zh: 項目把居民需要放在最重要、最顯著的位置。

options.en: The project treats residents’ needs as an irrelevant detail.
options.zh: 項目把居民需要當作無關細節。

options.en: The project guarantees every resident agrees with every decision.
options.zh: 項目保證每位居民都同意每個決定。

scene.explanationZh: 會議與報告反覆凸顯議題，支持重視的抽象用法；不保證人人同意。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個安排最不符合 front and centre？

options.en: A key date appears in a large heading at the start.
options.zh: 關鍵日期在開頭用大標題顯示。

options.en: A policy repeatedly makes user safety its main focus.
options.zh: 政策反覆把使用者安全作為主要重點。

options.en: Important support information is buried in a hard-to-find footnote.
options.zh: 重要支援資訊埋在難找的註腳裏。

contrast.explanationZh: 難以找到的註腳與凸顯內容相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「我們把安全放最顯著位置，就不用考慮費用了吧？」哪句最準確？

options.en: Safety can be front and centre while we still consider cost and practicality.
options.zh: 安全可以是最顯著的重點，同時仍考慮費用與實際可行性。

options.en: A prominent priority removes every other consideration.
options.zh: 只要一個重點顯著，所有其他考慮都會消失。

options.en: Front and centre only means the middle of a physical room.
options.zh: front and centre 只表示房間實際正中央。

dialogue.explanationZh: 凸顯某重點不等於只准考慮一件事，也可用於抽象議題。

speaking.en: We keep students’ needs front and centre when planning the course.
speaking.zh: 籌劃課程時，我們把學生需要放在最顯著的位置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明籌劃時凸顯甚麼重點。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你改進活動網頁，想讓訪客一開頁就看見交通及無障礙資訊，並在開頭清楚列出。用一至兩句英文說明設計重點。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出明確凸顯的方法與目的，避免只說幾何位置，也不用保證所有人都會接受。

examples.en: We will put access information front and centre so visitors can plan their journey easily.
examples.zh: 我們會把到達及無障礙資訊放在最顯著位置，讓訪客容易規劃行程。

examples.en: The new page keeps practical travel details front and centre, rather than hiding them below unrelated news.
examples.zh: 新頁面把實用交通資料放在最顯著位置，而不是藏在無關消息下面。

takeaways.en: The new design puts essential information front and centre.
takeaways.zh: 新設計把必要資訊放在最顯著位置。

takeaways.en: We keep fairness front and centre without ignoring practical limits.
takeaways.zh: 我們把公平放在最重要位置，同時不忽略實際限制。
